chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Lunceford's alto and sax section: Willie Smith and Hilton Jefferson
summary: McRae rates Willie Smith, Chauncey Haughton and Hilton Jefferson against Johnny Hodges and Benny Carter.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: You say Trummy was still --
Trummy was still --
Everybody was there. Wilcox -- all the guys was there.
Was Stan Grissom --
Oh, my goodness, yeah.
Benny Waters?
Yeah.
Was Willie in the band -- Willie Smith?

Willie Smith was my sweetheart, man. He was some -- Now you talk about an alto player, that is one of the greatest alto players. They named him and Johnny Hodges two of the greatest that ever lived. Willie Smith and Johnny Hodges and Chauncey Horton. Chick's tenor player --
Chauncey Horton.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Chauncey Horton was a master. Chauncey Horton was in a class with Benny Carter.
Hilton Jefferson was supposed to be one of the finest in the world. He played beautiful things. He played -- oh, man. You ought to hear him play "Smoke Gets In Your Eyes"
To me, he was the more unique alto player than all those guys. He was in a class of his own. He was a style of his own.
Just like whatchacalllem, but a more musical style. He wasn't a stylist like Johnny Hodges, the one with Jimmy Lunceford or Benny Carter.
See, Chauncey Horton and Benny Carter are more technical alto players. They know so much about the horn. They learned that.
You know, it comes out in their playing. You know, it's more technical.
But melodical playing, things that would please you, you say, oh, man listen to that, you know.
You would love whatchacalllem.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Johnny Hodges or Willie Smith.

You would love them. But the most one you would like most would be Hilton Jefferson. If you was standing in front of Chick and hear this guy play, you would like him. Because I hear Hilton play some things with Cab's band, man, I say, 'Oh (inaudible). He was just something else. Beautiful! Now he used to play Edgar Sampson things and make them come to life, man. He used to make them come to life.
